newsitem.title: USA: Natuna Gas plan based on 2003 output-Exxon.
newsitem.headline: Natuna Gas plan based on 2003 output-Exxon.

text.p: Exxon Corp said the project execution plan developed for the Natuna Gas Project is based on natural gas deliveries starting in 2003.
"However, the pace of development could be adjusted to produce gas on a time schedule consistent with customer requirements," the company said in a statement.

It holds a 50 percent interest in the Natuna production sharing contract and is operator of the project. Pertamina, Indonesia's national oil and gas company, holds a 24 percent interest and Mobil Corp holds the remaining 26 percent interest.
"While encouraging discussions are progressing with potential Natuna (natural) gas buyers, agreement to sell and purchase gas has not yet been reached," Exxon said.

"Nonetheless, plans for the project have progressed to the point where it is appropriate to communicate additional information to representatives of the Indonesian and international oil and gas contracting and supplier industry."
At a briefing for more than 300 potential contracting and supply firms, the project's owners discussed near-term activities that will involve opportunities for contractors and suppliers, Exxon said.
The Natuna Gas Project will develop the significant natural gas resources contained in the Natuna Field located in the Natuna Sea, about 135 miles (225 kilometers) northeast of Natuna Island.

The Natuna Field is one of the largest natural gas fields in the world with total estimated gas-in-place of 222 trillion cubic feet and recoverable hydrocarbons of 46 trillion cubic feet. Development plans include a multi-platform offshore complex for production along with a natural gas transportation system.
